text:
MPC rose modestly today after climbing 8.9% over the past two weeks, riding gains from Middle East tensions that have kept oil prices elevated and U.S. refineries running near full capacity (97.8%). The refiner benefits directly when crude oil prices rise—the gap between what it pays for oil and what it sells refined products for typically widens—and geopolitical friction in the Middle East, including Saudi pipeline attacks and Houthi advances threatening Red Sea shipping routes, has sustained upward pressure on energy markets despite a slight dip in prices on Friday.

The two-week rally reflects a broader energy sector move tied to genuine supply concerns: attacks on Saudi infrastructure and threats to a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments have kept investors focused on refining as a hedge against further disruption. With U.S. refineries already maxed out and storage levels moderate, any sustained production loss in the Middle East would tighten margins further.
